CHANGES (list ALL modifications, one or multiple):

Change #1: [Category: Model Architecture]
- What: Modify only model_design: replace each block’s first pointwise mixer with an H-to-2H projection, split its output into value and gate tensors, and compute GELU(value) multiplied by sigmoid(gate) before the existing dropout and second convolution.
- Why: This introduces content-dependent gating so the causal convolutional backbone can suppress irrelevant historical features while retaining useful item transitions.

---

WHY current solution limited:
- Root cause: The current blocks lack a separate learned gate controlling which temporal features enter subsequent processing; indiscriminate feature propagation is a hypothesis to test.
- Evidence: The supplied implementation uses an H-to-H mixer followed by GELU, and its validation HR@10 is 0.625; these establish the architectural limitation and comparison score, but do not prove gating will improve ranking.

HOW these changes address it:
- Mechanism: A separate sigmoid gate can attenuate temporal features according to sequence content while preserving the existing causal receptive field and residual path.
- Expected improvement: Target a validation HR@10 increase of 0.005–0.020 over 0.625, treated as an experimental hypothesis; each additional hit among 200 validation users changes HR@10 by 0.005.
- Synergy (if multiple changes): Not applicable; evaluate this single architectural change in one candidate slot.

KEEP UNCHANGED (must explicitly list):
- Random seed: 2024; validation negative-sampling seed: 42.
- Data split: Identical to parent, including the same 200 validation users and 99 sampled negatives per user.
- Hyperparameters: MAXLEN=128, HIDDEN_UNITS=64, NUM_BLOCKS=8, KERNEL_SIZE=3, DROPOUT_RATE=0.2, LR=0.001, WEIGHT_DECAY=0.0, BATCH_SIZE=128.
- Backbone: Depthwise causal convolutions, dilation schedule, second pointwise mixer, residual connections, normalization, padding masks, embeddings, and candidate scoring.
- Host components: Preprocessing, BPR loss, Adam, clipping, epochs, negative sampling, checkpoint selection, and evaluation.
- Contract: Preserve all required interfaces, imports, and source restrictions; produce one NextItNet without ensembling.
